summary: The enterprise AI model API aggregator landscape in 2026 is dominated by the three major hyperscalers — AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI/Foundry, and Google Vertex AI — each offering managed access to multiple foundation models within the customer's own cloud security perimeter. These platforms are considered mature and enterprise-grade with no single winner, only a best fit based on existing cloud footprint, model preference, and compliance needs. A second tier of data-platform-native and specialized aggregators (Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx, Databricks, Cloudflare, Oracle) targets customers who want AI brought to where their data already lives.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: prompts and completions stay within the company's existing cloud tenant/VPC and are not used to train vendor models, satisfying strict data-governance requirements.
Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and regional data-sovereignty guarantees, reducing procurement and audit burden.
Single billing and existing cloud contracts: usage draws down committed spend (EDP/MACC) and consolidates onto one invoice instead of signing separate agreements with each model vendor.
Model choice behind one API: a single API and SDK provides access to Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT and others, avoiding lock-in to a single model family and simplifying model switching.
Integrated enterprise tooling: native IAM, VPC endpoints, audit logging, guardrails, RAG, fine-tuning, and observability that plug into the company's existing cloud security and MLOps stack.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service / Azure AI Foundry
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; draws down Microsoft Azure consumption commitment.
key_features: Content filtering and Azure AI guardrails
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first shops wanting first-party OpenAI models with deep M365, Azure, and enterprise security integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; serverless with no infrastructure to manage; draws down AWS EDP commitment.
platforms.best_for: AWS-native enterprises wanting the widest model choice, especially Claude and Llama, behind a single managed API.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI / Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token plus Generative AI Scale Units (GSUs) for reserved throughput (e.g. 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash ≈ 67,250 tokens/sec sustained).
key_features: Grounding and RAG with Vertex AI Search
platforms.best_for: Google Cloud customers and data/ML-heavy teams wanting Gemini plus third-party models with strong MLOps and data-science tooling.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Snowflake credits; billed by tokens/compute within the customer's Snowflake account.
key_features: LLMs run inside the Snowflake governance boundary
No data movement out of the warehouse
Role-based access control and masking policies
platforms.best_for: Data-centric enterprises wanting AI applied directly to governed data already in Snowflake without ETL or data egress.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Subscription and consumption-based (Resource Units); available on IBM Cloud, on-premises, and hybrid deployments.
key_features: watsonx.governance for model risk and audit
watsonx Orchestrate for agent management across platforms
Open Granite models with IP indemnification
Named 2026 Gartner MQ Leader for DSML Platforms
platforms.best_for: Regulated industries and hybrid/on-prem enterprises prioritizing governance, explainability, and multi-platform agent management.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); pay-per-token Foundation Model APIs and provisioned throughput.
key_features: Models run within the Lakehouse and Unity Catalog governance
platforms.best_for: Lakehouse and data-engineering teams building custom and fine-tuned models governed alongside their data.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-character/token on-demand plus dedicated AI clusters for reserved capacity; integrates with OCI Universal Credits.
key_features: RAG via OCI Generative AI Agents
platforms.best_for: Oracle-centric enterprises and ERP/database customers needing sovereign regions and dedicated model isolation.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
available_models: catalog of open-source models at the edge
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go priced in 'Neurons' (compute units); low-cost serverless edge inference with a free tier.
key_features: Serverless inference at the global edge
AI Gateway for caching, rate limiting, and logging
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing fast, low-cost, globally distributed edge inference with open models rather than frontier proprietary LLMs.
